Command: Do not leave the meat of the festival offering until the morning
Summary: The meat of the festival sacrifice offered at Passover must be eaten the same night and none left until morning.
Commandment: Do not leave any of the meat of the festival sacrifice until the morning.
Application: The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. The same-night rule kept the festival meal within its appointed night, as with the Passover lamb itself.
Purpose: Scripture's stated context: the festival sacrifice is eaten at its appointed feast (Deuteronomy 16:4).
Function: The meat of the festival sacrifice offered at Passover had to be eaten the same night, none left until morning — a ceremonial law of the one night. Its goal was to keep the festival meal within its appointed night, as with the Passover lamb itself. It did not address a particular evil; its work was order and remembrance, not restraint. The same-night rule said the feast was a night's meal, not a week's leftovers, and the morning found the sacrifice finished.
